question: Who Owns Waffle House?
quick_answer: Waffle House is privately owned and has been family-run since it started. It was co-founded in 1955 in Avondale Estates, Georgia, by Joe Rogers Sr. and Tom Forkner, and the Rogers family has kept it private ever since. It does not trade on a stock exchange, so there are no public shares.
key_facts: Co-founders: Joe Rogers Sr. and Tom Forkner
Privately owned, mainly by the Rogers family
Headquartered in the Atlanta, Georgia area

body.heading: Who owns Waffle House?
body.text: Waffle House is a private, family-controlled company. It has stayed in the hands of its founding families, led by the Rogers family, rather than selling to outside investors or listing on the stock market. That is why you cannot buy Waffle House stock.

body.heading: How it started
body.text: The first Waffle House opened in 1955 in Avondale Estates, Georgia, started by neighbors Joe Rogers Sr. and Tom Forkner. Rogers came from the restaurant side and Forkner from real estate, and together they built a 24-hour diner concept that spread across the American South.

body.heading: Still private today
body.text: Decades later, Waffle House remains privately held and family-led, with its headquarters in the Atlanta area. Staying private has let the company keep its own culture, including the always-open model it is famous for.

faqs.a: No. Waffle House is privately owned by its founding families, led by the Rogers family, and has never gone public.
